label: The keyed lane resolves the document path and score before the scope test, and the test is a bare continue, so the out-of-scope tally is one Map increment at that line.
The lookup answer object is a fixed camelCase shape of ten keys; a nullable outOfScope key fits additively and cannot disturb a reader of named fields.
The only in-process consumer of the lookup module imports loadIndex alone, and generate-trigger-index.mjs does the same, so no production caller reads the answer object.
No test passes --spec-folder to the CLI, and the scoped unit tests assert named fields (results, candidatePhraseCount) rather than Object.keys, so an additive nullable field breaks nothing.
rg-wrapper.mjs has no scope concept: parseArgs accepts only --root and repeatable --search-root, so --scope is new surface and must be defined against --search-root rather than layered on it.

A complement pass is expressible with the wrapper's existing later-glob-wins ordering: appending --glob '!<scope>/**' after GLOBS yields the default roots minus the scope, and the path recipe already caps at one line per file.
The hint is dead on both lanes today: no caller passes --spec-folder to the lookup and the documented Gate 1 and /speckit:search forms are unscoped, while the ripgrep wrapper has no --scope at all.
Section 5's determinism clause binds the design: the hint must live outside the rank tuple, sort its tally deterministically, and never change results or exit status.
The out-of-scope hint never changes an exit status: a scoped miss stays exit 1 and a probe failure never escalates a successful scoped hit to exit 2.
The hint is reporting only: it never enters the rank tuple, never reorders results, and both tallies sort by count descending then path in code-unit order.
